hypothesis: A context-dependent UPDATE can change the retrieval of earlier facts when a temporal statement refers back to an earlier event. Compare the checkpoint skills refine_temporal_details_with_context and capture_temporal_context at the last write, with the same complete pre-write memory, ordered K=3, writer, source and reader.
common_slots: Require a generic insert in the two fixed slots, no preexisting source rule in either fixed slot, and neither focal skill duplicated there. In both arms attach dated_single_turns to the same generic insert slot and use the native focal skill template without a source rule. The executor computes the set of source rules across insert slots. Before permitting the update arm, replay the temporal control: verify archived writer prompt hashes, responses, parsed actions, applied changes, ordered bank, every read prompt, answer, token count, indices and F1. Preserve ineligible and unmatched windows with reasons. Record parse/application faults and score the actual resulting bank in the update arm. Report how often an UPDATE actually changes an older memory.
source_policy: Use only anonymized Qwen turn embeddings in the previous and current sessions and the visible utterance texts. Find current utterances with an explicit temporal or correction cue, removing calendar dates from headers by using the utterance body only. Score the mean of their top three strongest cross-session maximum cosine similarities (or all eligible if fewer). Calibrate using median/IQR on eligible session-5/7 training windows excluding the target history, clip the standardized score to [-1,1] and multiply by 2. An empty cue set or zero IQR yields a neutral zero offset. Freeze sigmoid(offset) before collecting new writers. Compare it with the native conditional checkpoint probability, native-plus-offset, matched usage, fixed skills and a sham that substitutes a fixed different training history's session-5 prefix for the actual preceding session. No target benchmark QA, answer, or evidence label enters choice.
cohort: Exploratory 12 early windows / 91 questions (fixed temporal first write) plus all 25 later randomized-terminal windows / 209 questions across 6 training histories (retain their originally assigned first write). Report early and later panels separately, including status coverage, per-history and per-type returns, whether the annotated evidence lies only in the older session, and physical edited references. Use the archived original randomized population even if changing the matched denominator would improve F1. Report interim results as such.
decision: This measures the opportunity provided by a real new action from the existing bank. A learnable action must produce reproducible, matched operational differences on >=90% of eligible question mass, +.02 held-later F1 over native, positive gains over matched use and shuffled-prefix policies, and benefits in at least 4 histories before independent development. Matched returns are candidate training data. A changed answer earns additional selection credit only after separate same-skill write and retrieval repair tests. Full-history LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S tests remain required.
